claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
As-built versions of this alloy typically exhibit columnar or equiaxed grain morphologies.
Tailoring laser scanning parameters can produce predominantly columnar and predominantly equiaxed microstructures in this alloy.
The proposed equiaxed microstructure has a higher grain-boundary density than the proposed columnar microstructure.
Grain boundaries act as preferential diffusion pathways for reactive species.
Increasing grain-boundary density accelerates ingress of oxidizing species.
Increasing grain-boundary density accelerates ingress or transport of reducing species.
Faster transport along grain boundaries intensifies intergranular oxidation or reduction.
Localized intergranular chemical attack weakens grain boundaries and embrittles the alloy.
Chemical weakening of grain boundaries accelerates crack initiation and propagation.
Accelerated intergranular cracking can ultimately trigger catastrophic failure during high-temperature reactive-gas exposure.
Equiaxed samples will show deeper penetration of reactive species than columnar samples.
Equiaxed samples will show more pronounced intergranular oxidation or reduction than columnar samples.
Equiaxed samples will develop a higher crack density than columnar samples.
Equiaxed samples will fail catastrophically earlier than columnar samples.
The proposed grain-boundary-controlled mechanism is expected to dominate around 700 °C after 100–200 hours in oxidizing or reducing reactive gases.
Residual stress and porosity may confound the relationship between grain-boundary density and degradation.
